null_model.interpretation: The composite is prior-dominated rather than topology-sensitive: the shuffle perturbs graph edges, but the ranking is driven mainly by evidence grade and plausibility, which the shuffle leaves intact for the classes whose evidence is rule/chemotype/text-based. We report this as a limitation of the composite and do not use the ranking as evidence of graph structure.
null_model.detail: plant↔use (treats) edges shuffled across taxa, understudied-lead discovery re-run per shuffle, combined with the shuffle-invariant classes. score_drop = 1 − mean(composite_shuffled)/mean(composite_real); CI is the 2.5–97.5 percentile over shuffles. A small drop means the composite is prior-dominated, which is a finding about the scorer, not a hidden failure.
